dimension: Admin / super-admin surface — app/(admin)/admin/** and app/api/admin/** (25 pages, 62 route files, ~6,400 lines of page code)
verification_notes: Verified against live prod (qztcgryhoanennsizcll) via direct SQL (mcp Supabase execute_sql) and, for the round-trip/pool-serialization claims, an external Node process using the app's own DATABASE_URL/pg client options (node_modules/pg 8.20.0). Repo checked at origin/main (689c4cc). Open PRs #147 (Fionas SMS script), #148 (loan-rate unit sweep, migration 168) and #149 (migration 169 search_path) touch only scripts/, app/(dashboard)/loans+accounting, lib/email/templates, lib/validators/loan.schema.ts and supabase/migrations — none intersect app/(admin)/** or app/api/admin/**, so none of the 15 findings below are pre-empted by them. pg_stat_statements on this project is shared/cumulative across whatever other sessions and audit agents are hitting the same prod DB concurrently, which explains one drifted secondary statistic (finding 14).

verified.title: Every admin endpoint's Promise.all runs serially on one connection — /api/admin/dashboard costs multiple sequential round-trips
verified.evidence: Mechanism confirmed by reading node_modules/pg/lib/client.js:579-600 (_pulseQueryQueue only submits the next query once readyForQuery===true) and lib/db/index.ts:172-187 (withAdminDb hands ONE pool.connect() client to the callback, wraps BEGIN/COMMIT — exact lines match). I then ran the identical getPlatformStats 7-query SQL set (matches admin.service.ts:199-262 verbatim) from an external Node process against the SAME live prod DB, using the app's actual DATABASE_URL and SSL config: serial BEGIN+Promise.all(7)+COMMIT averaged 1668ms over 2 warm trials (cold trial 3111ms); the identical 7 statements sent as one batched round trip averaged 563ms (570/556ms) over 2 warm trials — ratio ≈ 2.96x, not the claimed 9.7x. I independently reproduced the exact pg 8.20.0 DeprecationWarning ('Calling client.query() when the client is already executing a query is deprecated...'). A control probe of 4x SELECT pg_sleep(0.5) via Promise.all on one client took 2776-4443ms (would be ~500ms if parallel) — this proves strict serialization, independent of the specific ratio. getMonitoringDashboardData's Promise.all (admin.service.ts:379) destructures exactly 6 items, confirming its 8-round-trip claim (BEGIN+6+COMMIT).
verified.impact: The serialization is real, structural, and applies broadly (spot-checked 2 of the ~13 cited call sites plus the withAdminDb primitive itself — all matched). It is a genuine multi-x latency tax on every admin page load and does sit on pg's v9 removal list. But the specific '9.7x' / '2612ms vs 269ms' numbers are not reproducible under matched methodology from this verifier's network path: I measured ~3x (1668ms vs 563ms) running the exact same SQL against the same DB. Note also .env.local's DATABASE_URL actually points at Supabase's port-6543 transaction-mode pooler, which lib/db/index.ts's own comments explicitly say NOT to use for this reason — a real, unflagged inconsistency that makes any single absolute-latency number (mine or the finder's) environment-dependent and not a stable fact to cite precisely.
verified.recommendation: Same as originally proposed: merge independent scalar/rollup queries (getPlatformStats, getBillingOverview, getPlatformAnalytics, getMonitoringDashboardData) into one statement via CTEs/scalar subqueries. Do not leave the current shape — it is real, just not an exact-9.7x problem. Separately worth flagging: confirm whether production's real DATABASE_URL (Vercel env, not .env.local) actually uses the session-mode 5432 pooler the code comments require.
verified.note: Downgraded from CONFIRMED to OVERSTATED solely because the headline multiplier (9.7x) does not reproduce — I measured ~3x with the identical query set, the app's real connection config, and a live re-run of the same DB. The underlying mechanism, the deprecation-warning risk, and the architectural recommendation all stand confirmed.

verified.title: /admin/analytics 'Top Groups by Contributions' still has the SQL join fan-out PR #105 fixed everywhere else — live values inflated 20x and 30x, ranking wrong
verified.evidence: getPlatformAnalytics's topGroups query (lib/services/admin.service.ts, confirmed on origin/main around lines 1315-1329) is exactly the flat three-child LEFT JOIN (group_members, contributions, loans) with GROUP BY g.id that the adjacent listGroups/getGroupById comments (same file, ~lines 589-665) explicitly warn against. I ran the query verbatim against prod and independently against a true per-group-subquery version: THE FIONA'S contributions 31,000.00 vs true 1,550.00 (exactly 20.0x); loan_book 32,100,000.00 vs true 1,070,000.00 (exactly 30.0x); CAPITAL POINT CHAMA 16,020.00 vs true 1,780.00 (exactly 9.0x); Joka Ezra 2,170.00 vs true 310.00 (exactly 7.0x) — every ratio matches the finding to the decimal.
verified.impact: Confirmed and, if anything, understated: the buggy query's ORDER BY contributions DESC ranks THE FIONA'S (31,000 fabricated) above CAPITAL POINT CHAMA (16,020 fabricated), but the TRUE ranking is the reverse — CAPITAL POINT CHAMA (1,780 real) actually outranks THE FIONA'S (1,550 real). The chart's #1 and #2 slots are swapped, not just mislabeled with wrong numbers. This is the only chart on /admin/analytics, shown to super_admin.
verified.recommendation: Rewrite with the LATERAL-per-child-table pattern already used in listGroups a few dozen lines away. Pure SQL change, no schema/API impact.

verified.title: /admin/users renders 39 rows while telling the operator there are 36 — data query has no DISTINCT, count query does
verified.evidence: lib/services/admin.service.ts: the members list data query (lines 964-990, no de-dup) joins group_members with no DISTINCT; the count query at line 991 uses COUNT(DISTINCT m.id) over the same join — exact line match. Ran both live: data-shaped query returns 39 rows, count query returns 36. Identified the exact two duplicated members: Polycap Akoth (8b7114df-0585-4500-a0e2-8e52ab97e617) emits 3 rows, Ruth Wanyonyi (5eb868e6-d3b7-440e-949e-abdc2aa6c02d) emits 2 rows — byte-for-byte match to the finding's cited IDs. app/(admin)/admin/users/page.tsx:79 (totalPages = Math.ceil(total/25)) and :121 ('{total} total members across all organizations') both confirmed at those exact line numbers. getAdminMemberDetail's profile query (admin.service.ts, LIMIT 1 confirmed at line 1054) does pick an arbitrary one of a multi-membership member's groups.
verified.impact: Confirmed exactly as described: today the header undercounts by 3 and doubles up 2 real people in the list; once (data_rows − count) exceeds a page size the arithmetic silently drops real members from reachability. Multi-group registration (2026-08-15) is a live, growing feature, so this population only grows.
verified.recommendation: Pick one semantic (person-row vs membership-row) and make both queries agree; getAdminMemberDetail should take group_id as a parameter instead of LIMIT 1.

verified.title: No admin list route clamps `limit` — 12 routes pass raw query-string input into LIMIT, page=0 produces a negative OFFSET and a 500
verified.evidence: Ran `Math.min|Math.max` grep across all 62 files under origin/main's app/api/admin/** myself: zero matches, confirming the claim exactly. Individually inspected all 12 cited routes (groups, users, audit-logs, organizations, support, mpesa/unrouted, governance/alerts, organization/audit-logs, organization/disbursements, organization/groups, organization/members, organization/wallet) — every one does an unclamped parseInt on `limit` at the exact cited line numbers. Confirmed the tenant-route control: app/api/v1/mpesa/transactions/route.ts, sms/campaign/route.ts and treasury/external-funding/route.ts all DO clamp with Math.min(N, Math.max(1, parseInt(...))) verbatim. Ran `SELECT id FROM public.groups ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET -20` on prod and got the exact cited error: `ERROR: 2201X: OFFSET must not be negative`. grep for parsePagination/MAX_LIMIT across lib/ and app/ returns nothing.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: any of the 12 routes accepts an arbitrarily large `limit`, and `page=0` 500s the request after wasting a pooled connection. This is a real, admin-specific gap versus the tenant tree's house style.
verified.recommendation: Add a shared parsePagination helper clamping limit to [1,100] and page to >=1; apply to all 12 routes.

verified.title: listGroups' redundant GROUP BY forces an extra sort before the LIMIT
verified.evidence: Confirmed the GROUP BY at admin.service.ts:616 has no aggregate function in the SELECT list (every value comes from a LATERAL) — the mechanism is real and the plan shape is exactly as described: WITH GROUP BY produces an extra Group node plus an extra Sort-by-8-keys node before the outer sort; WITHOUT it, the same rows come from a single Sort. But re-running EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on prod myself, warm-cache, alternating order, 3 separate pairs of runs: with-GROUP-BY execution times were 0.702ms, 0.768ms, 0.442ms; without-GROUP-BY were 0.683ms, 0.633ms; ratio ≈1.0-1.2x, and the absolute difference is 0.02-0.15ms — not the claimed 5.6x / 85% / 2.83ms. At today's 9 groups the redundant node costs essentially nothing measurable above noise.
verified.impact: Real defect, negligible TODAY: at 9 groups the overhead I could measure is noise-level, not a meaningful fraction of a ~0.7ms query. The finder's growth argument (worse at 900 groups, since the Group node blocks LIMIT pushdown) is directionally plausible but was NOT tested at scale by either of us — it is a prediction, not a measured fact, and shouldn't be reported with the same confidence as the current-scale numbers.
verified.recommendation: Still worth doing as cheap hygiene: delete the GROUP BY at admin.service.ts:616. Low urgency given the current measured impact.
verified.note: Downgraded from medium to low and CONFIRMED→OVERSTATED because the specific magnitude claims (5.6x, 85% of execution time, 3.204ms/0.567ms) did not reproduce on 3 independent re-runs; I measured ~1.0-1.2x instead.

verified.title: /admin/support's three KPI tiles are computed in JavaScript over the current 20-row page, contradicting the queue-wide counts already computed in SQL
verified.evidence: app/(admin)/admin/support/page.tsx:87-89 confirmed verbatim: openCount/inProgressCount/slaBreached are all `items.filter(...)` over the current page (`items = data?.items ?? []` from a 20-row `useAdminTickets` call). StatCards render these at lines 129-136 (finding cited 127-138, close). The queue-wide FILTER-based counts do exist server-side (admin.service.ts ~241-248) and are used by the platform dashboard instead. Confirmed support_tickets currently has 0 live rows on prod, exactly as the finding states — so the divergence is real but not yet visible in production data.
verified.impact: Exactly as claimed: from the 21st ticket onward, or the moment any filter is applied, these three tiles will silently diverge from the dashboard's queue-wide SLA numbers — the number staff triage on.
verified.recommendation: Return queue-wide FILTER counts from GET /api/admin/support alongside items; delete the client-side filters.

verified.title: /admin/mpesa-unrouted 'Total value' sums only the visible 20 rows while the adjacent tile counts the whole queue
verified.evidence: app/(admin)/admin/mpesa-unrouted/page.tsx:88 confirmed verbatim (`items.reduce((sum,r)=>sum+Number(r.amount),0)` over a 20-row page); StatCard 'Unresolved' (queue-wide COUNT) and 'Total value' (page-only reduce) sit side by side at lines 150-151, exact match. listUnroutedPayments (admin.service.ts:1387-1417) confirmed to filter `u.resolved = false`. Ran the counts on prod: 12 total mpesa_unrouted rows, 0 with resolved=false — matches the finding's '12 rows, 0 unresolved' exactly, meaning the bug is real in code but not currently observable in live data.
verified.impact: As claimed: once the unresolved backlog exceeds 20 rows, 'Total value' will understate the true unreconciled amount and will shift as staff page/search — the worst failure direction for a reconciliation queue.
verified.recommendation: Add a SUM(amount) to listUnroutedPayments' existing count query (it already scans the filtered set) and render that.

verified.title: /admin/audit-logs fetches 200 fully-aggregated group rows for a filter dropdown, and its own list ships mostly-unrendered JSONB
verified.evidence: app/(admin)/admin/audit-logs/page.tsx:43 confirmed (`useAdminGroups({ limit: 200 })`, used only to populate `<option>` at lines 77-78) hits the same 5-LATERAL listGroups used elsewhere. admin.service.ts's audit-log list query does `SELECT al.*` (confirmed near line 1263) while AuditLogRow (page.tsx:13-22) declares only 8 non-JSONB fields. I independently measured on prod: SUM(pg_column_size(al.*)) = 811,464 bytes over 570 rows; old_values+new_values = 656,902 bytes → 80.95% ≈ 81.0% — matches the finding to the first decimal. Average row = 811,464/570 = 1,423.6 ≈ 1,424 bytes, matching exactly. MAX(pg_column_size(old_values)+pg_column_size(new_values)) = 2,114 bytes — an exact byte-for-byte match. pg_stat_statements shows the exact statement `SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM public.audit_logs al` at mean_exec_time=31.625ms, max_exec_time=70.322ms, calls=4 — matching the finding's '31.6ms / 70.3ms' to three significant figures.
verified.impact: Confirmed precisely as described — this is the most exactly-reproduced finding in the set. Both over-fetches (the 200-row group dropdown and the 81%-wasted JSONB payload) are real and measured, not merely plausible.
verified.recommendation: Add a minimal id/name-only group-options endpoint for pickers; replace `SELECT al.*` with the 7 rendered columns.

verified.title: GET /api/admin/sms-margin opens 4 concurrent database connections against a pool capped at 3, then renders up to 500 unpaginated rows
verified.evidence: app/api/admin/sms-margin/route.ts:26-30 confirmed verbatim: Promise.all of 4 independent smsMarginService calls, each its own withAdminDb (confirmed at sms-margin.service.ts:80, 155, 218, 254 — exact line match). DB_POOL_MAX=3 confirmed live in .env.local. getTopCustomers(limit=500) confirmed at sms-margin.service.ts:154; sms-pricing/page.tsx:365 confirmed rendering `margin.topCustomers.map(...)` with no pagination. I ran my own pool-queueing test against the live DB with max=3: occupying all 3 connections with 1s holds and requesting a 4th concurrently, the 4th's pool.connect() call blocked for 2,573ms before it got a client (total 2,853ms vs the ~1,000ms it would take if not queued) — directly reproducing the queueing mechanism the finding describes (my sleep duration differs from the finder's 500ms, so the absolute number differs, but the qualitative 'any 4th concurrent admin request self-queues behind the 3-connection cap' claim is independently confirmed).
verified.impact: Confirmed: this route structurally always self-queues one of its four sub-requests, and while it holds 4-of-3 slots (functionally) it can starve the second concurrent request the same page fires. The 500-row unpaginated render is a real, matching silent-truncation risk.
verified.recommendation: Share one withAdminDb transaction across the four reads (3 already take a client-shaped `db` param); paginate topCustomers server- and client-side.

verified.title: Six admin search boxes fire a request per keystroke — no debounce anywhere except the command palette
verified.evidence: Grepped the whole repo myself: useDebouncedValue (hooks/use-debounced-value.ts:5) has exactly one caller, command-palette.tsx:29 (`useDebouncedValue(query, 250)`) — confirmed. Independently searched for the un-debounced setSearch pattern and got exactly the 6 files the finding names: users, support, organizations, audit-logs, groups, mpesa-unrouted — confirmed users/page.tsx:131 sets state directly on every keystroke with no debounce. proxy.ts:29 confirmed `RL_LIMIT_USER = 240` (requests per window per authenticated user) verbatim.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: each of the 6 un-debounced inputs turns typing into one HTTP round trip per keystroke, each costing the full BEGIN+data+count+COMMIT shape; the /admin/groups picker also carries the heavy 5-LATERAL aggregate per keystroke. The 240 req/60s ceiling makes sustained typing + background polling a real path to the same class of failure PR #113 fixed.
verified.recommendation: Wrap all 6 inputs in useDebouncedValue(search, 300), following the command-palette pattern exactly.

verified.title: /admin/risk 'KYC pending' displays the query's LIMIT, not a real count — shows 9 on prod when the true figure is 2
verified.evidence: Confirmed exactly: admin.service.ts:109 computes the correct `pendingKyc = groups.filter(g.onboarding_status!=='active').length` and returns it in the payload at line 131, but kycQueue (lines 111-125) maps ALL fetched groups (LIMIT 12, no status filter) with no further filtering. app/(admin)/admin/risk/page.tsx:88 confirmed rendering `kyc.length` (the unfiltered array), not `data.summary.pendingKyc`. Ran `SELECT status, onboarding_status, COUNT(*) FROM groups GROUP BY 1,2` on prod myself: {pending_verification/deactivated: 2, active/active: 7} — total 9 groups. Since 9 ≤ the LIMIT 12, the tile reads 9 today (all groups) against a true pending count of 2 — exact match to the finding's numbers.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described, including the forward-looking risk: since the query is an unconditional LIMIT 12 sorted by creation date, once the platform exceeds 12 groups the tile mathematically freezes at exactly 12 regardless of the real KYC backlog.
verified.recommendation: Render the already-computed `data.summary.pendingKyc`; filter the queue query itself to onboarding_status <> 'active' with real pagination.

verified.title: /admin/organizations/[id] fires 4 API calls on mount and ships an unbounded assigned-group list plus a 500-option <select>
verified.evidence: app/(admin)/admin/organizations/[id]/page.tsx:77-93 confirmed verbatim — 4 independent hooks (useAdminOrganization, useOrgStaff, useOrgInvitations, useOrganizationPlan). admin-organizations.service.ts's detail function (lines 141-194) confirmed as a 4-query Promise.all: assignedGroups query (~150-175) has no LIMIT at all and carries 2 LATERAL aggregates per row; assignableGroups (176-186) confirmed `LIMIT 500` with no search filter. page.tsx:377 (`assigned.map(...)`) and :659 (`assignable.map(...)` inside a plain select) both confirmed at those exact lines. memberReach client-side reduce over the full assigned list confirmed verbatim at page.tsx:142.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: 6 sequential DB round trips for the detail call alone plus 3 more HTTP requests before any interaction; an organization with many groups would serialize its entire unbounded group list with per-group aggregates into one response, and the 500-cap on assignableGroups silently hides any unassigned group beyond it.
verified.recommendation: Paginate assignedGroups; make the assignableGroups fetch a searched, dialog-gated lookup instead of an unconditional pre-fetch.

verified.title: The three polling admin dashboards have Redis TTLs shorter than their own client poll interval, guaranteeing a cache miss on every scheduled refetch
verified.evidence: Confirmed all six cited numbers exactly at their cited lines: admin.service.ts:199 TTL=90s (platform-stats), :294 TTL=60s (risk-dashboard), :378 TTL=20s (monitoring-dashboard); hooks/use-admin.ts:164-165 staleTime=60_000/refetchInterval=120_000; app/(admin)/admin/risk/page.tsx:55-56 and app/(admin)/admin/monitoring/page.tsx:45-46 both staleTime=60_000/refetchInterval=120_000 — all exact matches. 120s > 90s, 120s > 60s, 120s > 20s in all three cases, as claimed.
verified.impact: Confirmed: for the realistic single-admin-viewer traffic shape, every one of the three caches has already expired by the time the next poll fires, so none of them can ever serve a hit for their own scheduled refetch.
verified.recommendation: Raise each TTL past its poll interval (e.g. 150s for a 120s poll), or lower the poll interval to match the TTL where freshness (not caching) was the real intent (monitoring's 20s).

verified.title: POST /api/admin/governance/compute is an unbounded serial loop — one connection per group, ~19 queries per group, no maxDuration
verified.evidence: governance.service.ts:405-420 confirmed verbatim: a plain `for (const group of groups)` loop, each iteration its own `withAdminDb(...)` call, errors caught into a `failed` counter (not re-thrown). computeGroupGovernanceSnapshot's Promise.all (confirmed lines 258-283) destructures exactly 19 named results — matches 'NINETEEN queries' exactly. app/api/admin/governance/compute/route.ts confirmed to have no `maxDuration` export. I queried pg_stat_statements myself: the per-group account-balance query (getAccountBalanceAsOf) shows calls=850, mean_exec_time=0.102033915294118ms — an exact match to the finding's '850 calls at mean 0.102ms'. However, the governance_health_scores INSERT shows calls=61, mean_exec_time=0.440ms in my query — NOT the claimed '1,700 calls at mean 0.189ms'. This is also internally inconsistent with the finder's own account-balance number: each snapshot computation calls getAccountBalanceAsOf 9 times but INSERTs exactly once, so INSERT calls should be roughly 1/9th of account-balance calls, not double them as 1,700-vs-850 would imply. pg_stat_statements on this shared prod project accumulates across whatever else is querying it concurrently (including other audit sessions), so some drift is expected, but the internal inconsistency suggests that specific number was wrong even at the time it was recorded.
verified.impact: The architectural claim is sound and independently confirmed: server-side execution is sub-millisecond per query (both re-measured numbers show this), so wall-clock time is dominated by round trips; the loop has no batching, no resume point, and swallows per-group failures — it will genuinely time out well before completing at a few hundred groups, with no way to resume.
verified.recommendation: Collapse the 19 per-group reads into one CTE-based round trip; batch groups with a resumable cursor; add an explicit maxDuration to the route.
verified.note: One supporting statistic (INSERT call count) does not reproduce and appears to have been wrong in the original evidence — corrected here. The core structural finding is unaffected by that correction.

verified.title: Five backoffice route files (135 lines, 9 handlers) have zero callers anywhere in the app
verified.evidence: Counted the 5 files myself: app/api/admin/policies/route.ts (30 lines), policies/loan/route.ts (26), policies/loan-terms/route.ts (26), policies/posting-templates/route.ts (27), governance/compute/route.ts (26) — sums to exactly 135 lines, matching the finding precisely. Handler count: policies/route.ts (GET+PUT), loan/route.ts (GET+PUT), loan-terms/route.ts (GET+PUT, confirmed verbatim including the double withAdminDb call — write then read-back, lines 20-25), posting-templates/route.ts (GET+PUT), governance/compute/route.ts (POST) = 9 handlers, matching exactly. Searched the whole repo for callers of 'admin/policies' outside app/api/admin/**: only the routes' own doc comments and audit docs. app/(admin)/admin/settings/page.tsx confirmed to be 79 lines of account info + sign-out, no policy UI. loanPolicyService.getPlatformTerms/setPlatformTermsDefault confirmed to exist in lib/services/loan-policy.service.ts. A SEPARATE, independently-produced finder file in this same audit run (dead-weight-and-structural-duplication dimension) independently flags the identical 4 policy routes plus governance/compute as unreachable — cross-validation from an unrelated finding pass.
verified.impact: Confirmed as described: 9 live, super_admin-gated, unreachable handlers, independently corroborated by a second finder working a different dimension of the same audit.
verified.recommendation: Wire the missing /admin/settings UI (services already exist and work) or delete the routes; governance/compute is the cheapest to wire (one button on /admin/risk).
